annotation:
This 4:33 version of [https://musicbrainz.org/work/df9b7bfa-9dfd-3377-902e-cec25d861d31|All Is Full of Love] is a remix by [https://musicbrainz.org/artist/522b0135-00dd-4307-adce-2bf7d51a253f|Howie B] used on the album [https://musicbrainz.org/release-group/810272e0-aef1-3d85-b2d3-e512e87fc38c|Homogenic].

This is different to the [https://musicbrainz.org/recording/aa2532b5-abf5-4bcf-b1cf-2dcc1a5e90c9|original Mark Stent mix] that was used on the [https://musicbrainz.org/recording/669ffd93-b46a-4787-9b09-806b69ae2bf5|video],  [https://musicbrainz.org/release-group/3f9c1bf3-ff34-3691-9da3-5cd395b81cf9|singles] and [https://musicbrainz.org/release-group/07d2f772-531d-3d19-920a-72337891800d|Greatest Hits].

Also note the recording on the original [https://musicbrainz.org/release/cfbb2f15-835b-4bee-abc1-df30d7e3a381|Japaness album] is 5:31 and includes a minute of silence after the track before the bonus tracks start.

title: Babies
annotation:
This is the 94 recording (2m30s: “''Aaoooh yeah''”).
Found in [https://musicbrainz.org/release-group/a0394996-0923-324b-a176-cc1a572cb9e4|''His ’n’ Hers''] album, [https://musicbrainz.org/release-group/8ee3c8da-69e2-377b-8741-c9f33c2e6960|''The Sisters EP''], [https://musicbrainz.org/release/eb18497b-b0ab-488f-96c0-b5b3cd30cd7e|''Common People '''’96'''''] single, [https://musicbrainz.org/release-group/7e8923d0-94e4-38c9-bf7f-3983382b696e|''Hits''] compilation, various artist compilations

There is also [https://musicbrainz.org/recording/6a9dca21-5b72-4b4c-9408-41e8a948cb90|an earlier pre-94 recording] (2m30s: “''Yeah''”).
Found in [https://musicbrainz.org/release-group/649b32e9-94e4-3f3c-be80-a246968b3e88|''Babies''] single, [https://musicbrainz.org/release-group/d1c45cae-66bb-35ed-9de2-0cc4bd064f11|''Intro''] compilation

The big difference is that, at 2m30s, Jarvis Cocker’s voice says “''Aaoooh yeah''” in the 94 recording, while it is more dry and just says “''Yeah''” in this pre-94 recording.

annotation: Less care was taken for this stereo mix than had been achieved for the previous mono mix. They allowed the double-tracking of John's voice to be heard even in the introduction, which has a somewhat out-of-sync beginning. They also forgot to correct Paul's flub in the second bridge, so anyone who spent the extra dollar for the stereo version of the American or British album got to hear Paul's voice crack embarrassingly towards the end of the song.

annotation:
"My Way" has English lyrics written by [http://musicbrainz.org/show/artist/?artistid=11617|Paul Anka] in 1968, set to an originally French song, "[http://musicbrainz.org/show/track/?trackid=11788316|Comme d'habitude]", that was composed by [http://musicbrainz.org/show/artist/?artistid=87761|Claude François] and [http://musicbrainz.org/show/artist/?artistid=516261|Jacques Revaux], and first recorded by François in 1967. "Comme d'habitude" has reputedly been recorded in more languages, by more artists than any other song in contemporary music history.

annotation:
This original, longer album version starts with a spoken 20 second intro:
''Truth is I thought it mattered. I thought that music mattered.  But does it bollocks.  Not compared to how people matter.''  (Danny\[https://musicbrainz.org/artist/36de52f1-f850-4c93-a7bd-d42dcfee92f7|Pete Postlethwaite] from the 1996 film Brassed Off)

This is trimmed from the [https://musicbrainz.org/recording/b54f79d8-f199-4d19-b8e9-7a56b62fe8ae|single / radio friendly] versions.

At around 4mins it kicks into a different tune before ending.  This is left off of the [https://musicbrainz.org/recording/09ae8fd7-6358-44b2-b7db-094be8ea511b|3:57 edits] that appears on compilation albums.
